title: Dust From Halley's Comet Hits Earth at 148,000 Miles an Hour

scenes.text: Every October, Earth runs into dust from Halley's Comet.
It slams into our atmosphere at about 41 miles per second.
The grains are tiny and crumbly, with about the strength of cigar ash.
They start burning up around 80 miles above your head.
So every shooting star you see in October is a piece of Halley's Comet, dying in a flash.

description:
Every October, Earth runs into dust left behind by Halley's Comet. It hits our atmosphere at about 41 miles per second.
Those bright streaks are called the Orionid meteor shower.
Have you ever seen a shooting star?
first_comment: Where were you the last time you saw a shooting star?
